design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (nfip_commercial_rcbap_claims), rework round 2
DRAW: draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5,5,4,5]; contents proof 5, contents payment 5, cancellation processing 4, refund 5.
WHY A GOOD TEST: a business that sold its building asks only for the unused premium on its federal flood policy. The agent must find that (1) the refund waits on the processed cancellation; (2) FEMA does not cancel a policy while a claim is open (FEMA TRRP Plan, cancellation reasons: 'Open Claim: Policy cannot be canceled'), and the August 27 claim was reopened by the October 8 SUPPLEMENTAL report on the stock; (3) closing it needs a contents payment, which waits on a supplemental contents proof the authorized signer must swear (owner=user write). Every number follows a real rule: the SFIP other-insurance condition the General Property Form carries (primary up to the other flood policy's deductible, then pro rata by amounts of insurance) against the BizFlood policy in force on the loss date; the federal minimum deductibles (44 CFR 61.5: 1,000 / 1,250 pairs by building limit); and the Flood Insurance Manual / TRRP refund types for a sale: pro rata for the term the cancellation falls in (premium with ICC, Reserve Fund and HFIAA; Federal Policy Fee and probation earned) and a full refund, fees and surcharges included, for any later term — the sale closed on 2026-09-04 and the policy had already renewed on 2026-09-15 on a renewal paid in August.
SCOPE: task 1 claims nfipcom_ext_contents_proof_amount, nfipcom_ext_contents_payment, nfipcom_ext_cancellation_credit, nfipcom_ext_cancellation_refund and their four tools; task 0 holds the building pair.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root nfipcom_ext_cancellation_refund <- nfipcom_ext_cancellation_credit (value_input, gate xr_risk; sentence: 'A cancellation refund is fixed only after the policy shows the cancellation processed on the signed request, cancelled with its cancellation effective date set.') <- nfipcom_ext_contents_payment (state_gate on nfipcom_claims.event_type; sentence: 'A cancellation is not processed until no claim on the policy is open, every coverage measured on the latest adjuster report for each date of loss on the policy carrying a payment or a written denial for that date of loss dated after that report.') <- nfipcom_ext_contents_proof_amount (value_input, gate cy_sworn; sentence: 'A contents payment on a claim is fixed only after the claim file carries a signed and sworn contents proof of loss received after the claim's latest adjuster report that measures a contents loss.'). Two value_input edges for three prerequisites. Unmet at opening: policy in force, no CANCELLATION credit; SUPPLEMENTAL 2026-10-08 with no payment after it; latest contents proof 2026-09-15. The open-claim state is reachable only through a payment (no denial tool in the difficulty), and the waited-on 'cancellation processed' state holds even when a credit is zero (zero credits are simply not booked).
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: proof deadline 2026-08-27 + 60 = 2026-10-26 (frozen 2026-10-14 inside). Cancellation gates (signed request on file, cancellable status, lender release only for payoff/voluntary/private/LOMA reasons) met; BUILDING_SOLD needs the closing disclosure, on file. The base claim bar is kept (stated in both rules); FULL_FROM_INCEPTION, PRO_RATA and the fee sentence are declared overwrites scoped by component (risk at processing; ICC, Reserve Fund, HFIAA, fees at disbursement), with the reach limited to the current term and the one before it (FEMA: current year and one prior year handled by the WYO, earlier terms through the NFIP Bureau). Mortgage-required: the processing records the cancellation notice to the mortgagee of record.
WORLD CONSISTENCY: every historical row is the base or extended rule applied on its day: the 2026 renewal capped at 18% over the re-rated 6,080 (7,174.40) while the bill showed the indicated 7,450 and was paid as billed (9,259.50), leaving 325.21 owed back; the endorsement and re-rate entries are base pro rata figures; proofs and payments were recomputed day by day with the extended claim rules (PRELIMINARY first filed under the duplicate number, so the first contents proof belongs there). The 2025 term was paid exactly; no unrefunded old balance remains.
FACTOR CARD (scratch evaluator on the check_compute engine):
 contents proof (18,000.00; all-baseline 131,500.00): report P -> SUPPLEMENTAL (0.00); ceiling P cross -> 150,000 statement value (43,000.00); deductible P -> 1,250 (18,750.00); already sworn on the claim M -> 42,000 (60,000.00); sworn under the duplicate number P -> 88,750 (106,750.00).
 contents payment (12,525.56; all-baseline 0.00): sworn total M (0.00); layer P cross MS -> 74,000 (42,334.35); building share P -> 36,800 (17,417.68); other cover P cross MS -> 150,000 (42,334.35); paid before P -> both numbers (96,358.89).
 cancellation (7,357.63; all-baseline 7,396.65): current term M -> full (7,573.84); previous term P -> 180.22 (7,177.41); endorsement M -> own period (7,351.62); re-rate P -> 9.04 (7,366.67).
 refund (9,485.73; all-baseline 9,036.64): ICC M -> 77.11 (9,485.88); Reserve Fund M -> 1,338.25 (9,491.70); Federal Policy Fee P -> 80.00 (9,405.73); probation P -> 50.00 (9,435.73); premium received but not owed P -> 325.21 (9,160.52).
 Near-misses: the BizFlood contents increase recorded 2026-08-20 but effective 2026-09-01; the BizFlood policy now cancelled (counted because it was in force on the loss date); the closing date vs the request receipt date; the 2025 and 2026 ICC figures (70 vs 75).
TIER TABLES: contents ceiling endorsed/SOV: a value endorsement in force on the loss date (the later-effective of the latest increase and the latest decrease among those effective on or before it); SOV/limit: in-force BizFlood declaring a contents value. deductible higher/lower minimum: building limit vs threshold. prior sworn (method: sum of sworn proofs / payments net of voids / none). duplicate: proofs under it / payments under it with no proof on either number / none. current term (method: full / nothing / pro rata) full vs pro rata: effective date before term_start; nothing vs pro rata: claim-barred reason with a paid current-term claim. previous term full/pro rata: effective date on or before vs after that term's start. endorsement (method: full / own period / with the term). re-rate (whole / own period / none). ICC (method: none / previous pro rata plus current full / current pro rata): ICC tier; effective before term_start. Reserve Fund (method: per-occasion / inception in full / pro rata). fees and probation (inception / later term in full / earned). excess (unbegun-term payment plus excess / excess / none).
FACTOR INDEPENDENCE: the cancellation effective date is a plain base sentence, read by the four cancellation factors; each factor reads its own ledger rows; the endorsement and re-rate entries are picked by their reference ids (scoped to that endorsement and that certificate); refund factors read the effective date the processing left on the policy (prerequisite output), never another factor's binding. Assembly order is stated once per policy.
PROBE TABLE: a second SOV scheduling the address (on the same or another BizFlood policy), or a second value increase or value decrease for the address -> the payment is nil and referred to the adjuster, the proof amount takes the policy's own replacement cost value or contents limit; an increase and a decrease effective the same day -> the one recorded later, the increase when recorded the same day; an in-force BizFlood policy scheduling the address with no adjuster report for the date of loss -> still other insurance, the V/VE layer taken on the SOV building and contents values for the location; a BizFlood term ended before the loss -> not in force; LOCATION_ADD/DELETE -> not value endorsements; a value increase in force on the loss date with a decrease effective after it -> the increase sets the limit; a BizFlood policy writing no building at the address -> the contents carry the whole layer; a voided claim payment -> not counted toward the claim bar; a MORTGAGEE_CHANGE -> books no charge, never the latest premium-bearing endorsement; an endorsement or certificate of an earlier term -> with that term (not returned) / nothing; a term-start or inception reason -> full-term tiers; claim bar: a paid loss dated after the month band around term_start -> bar; the latest loss ever paid dated in the band -> bar when on or after term_start with its payments standing, none when before term_start; a paid loss in the band that the records cannot place (the latest loss ever paid dated after the band with nothing paid net after the band, or in the band on or after term_start with its payments all voided) -> the current term's return is held, booked as zero by these credits, the other parts returned as worked out; duplicate notices of one loss -> treated as that one loss; a current and previous term carrying more than one premium-bearing endorsement or more than one re-rate credit -> the base refund method applies as written: fees fully earned, no premium received but not owed added, the refund the total of the credits (the booking, fee and assembly sentences name the in-scope case only); no future-term payment -> the unbegun-term tier does not apply; a PRELIMINARY filed the same day as the FINAL -> the FINAL governs; the claim bar on a current-term cancellation -> the current-term endorsement's risk premium and Reserve Fund Assessment are not returned either; an endorsement or certificate effective after the cancellation date -> its Reserve Fund Assessment charge returned, or its re-rate credit taken back, in full; a cancellation before term_start with no endorsement or re-rate in its term -> the current term's Reserve Fund Assessment in full less re-rate credits plus the term before it pro rata; a zero risk credit -> the refund reads the latest signed request; a second first notice under the same claim number -> not a duplicate claim number; an older signed request or a later withdrawn or unsigned one -> the refund reads the request its risk credit references and the reason the cancelled policy shows, the credit reads the latest signed request received on the policy; an overpayment already refunded -> not returned again. Rounding half-up at each component.
PERSONA: Corinne Fairbanks, managing member and authorized signer; asks only for the refund; gives phone 7135522093 and tax ID 2638 when asked; claim 2608552 and the October 8 adjuster visit only if asked about a claim; lender paid off at closing; premium paid by check; BizFlood cancelled at the sale; signs what is handed; closes on the refund confirmation.
STANDARD SOLUTION: locate, verify, read policy/requests/billing/changes/claims and BizFlood policy/changes/claims; hand the contents proof (18,000.00) to the signer; issue the contents payment 12,525.56; process the cancellation effective 2026-09-04 with risk credit 7,357.63; disburse ICC 77.11, RFA 1,338.25, HFIAA 257.53, FPF 80.00, probation 50.00 and the refund 9,485.73 to INSURED.
user_scenario: You are Corinne Fairbanks, the managing member of Fenwick Harbor Marine Supply, LLC, a marine supply business that until this month traded out of its own building at 248 Bradford Street, Kemah, TX 77565; it now runs from 212 Kipp Avenue. You are friendly, a little rushed, and you talk in short practical sentences; you are on the company's authorized-signer list for its Tidemark flood insurance. The company sold the Bradford Street building, and the sale closed on September 4, 2026. You signed a cancellation request for the building's federal flood policy and Tidemark received it with the closing statement on October 6. You are calling because you want the unused premium on that flood policy refunded to the company now that the building is sold. You are happy for the representative to take care of it for you; you do not want anything else changed. You have no idea what the refund should be and you will not guess; if asked what you expect, you say you are relying on Tidemark to work it out. Only when the representative asks you to confirm who you are do you give the company's phone number, 7135522093, and then, if asked for another detail, the last four digits of the company's tax ID, 2638. If asked for the policy number you read GP2318460 from the declarations page. If asked about the lender on the building, you say the Galveston Bay Commercial Bank loan was paid off out of the sale proceeds at closing. If asked who paid the flood premium, you say the company paid it by check, including the renewal bill in August. If asked whether there is a flood claim, you say there is a claim from the August 27 flood, number 2608552, that the stock loss is still being worked on, and that the adjuster came back on October 8. If asked about other flood insurance, you say the company had a BizFlood policy with Tidemark for the building, bought in January and cancelled when the building was sold. If the representative explains that something needs your signature or sworn statement as the authorized signer and hands it to you with the figures it states, you sign it exactly once as handed to you and read back what the confirmation shows. If the representative gives you any figure, you do not argue; you only ask them to repeat it so you can note it. When the representative tells you the refund has been issued and gives you its amount or reference, you note it, thank them and end the call.

edges.policy_source: A cancellation refund is fixed only after the policy shows the cancellation processed on the signed request, cancelled with its cancellation effective date set.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single chain: the contents proof before the contents payment, the payment before the cancellation (FEMA does not cancel a policy with an open claim), the cancellation before the refund.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the processed cancellation the refund reads no risk premium credit and works from the receipt date: 1,861.32 instead of 9,485.73, and the policy stays in force.

Processing the cancellation before the contents payment cancels a policy whose claim is still open, which the cancellation rule forbids; the terminal state would carry a cancellation recorded before the claim was closed.
Without the supplemental proof the sworn total stays at 130,750 and the payment is 0.00 instead of 12,525.56, so the SUPPLEMENTAL coverage stays open and the cancellation stays held.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller asks only for the refund of unused premium after the sale. She mentions the claim only if asked about one, and never mentions a proof of loss, an unpaid amount or that the claim must be settled first. The signing line is a passive reaction once the representative explains a signature is needed.
